'''FiPy: Finite Volume Phase-Field & Conservation PDE Solver'''
[[Category:Principia Machina]] [[Category:Tools]]

== Overview & Architectural Fit ==
'''FiPy''' is an open-source, object-oriented finite volume PDE solver developed in Python by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). It is engineered specifically for coupled, non-linear partial differential equations, phase-field models, and advection-diffusion-reaction dynamics.

== Mathematical Evaluation for TPM & SVD ==
* '''Conservation Law Enforcement (9.0/10):''' By utilizing the finite volume method (FVM), FiPy guarantees strict cell-by-cell numerical conservation of physical fluxes (charge, energy, momentum), directly upholding conservation laws required by Noether's theorems.
* '''Implicit & Explicit Coupled Solvers:''' Seamlessly handles stiff coupled non-linear PDE systems through underlying linear solvers (Trilinos, SciPy, PyAMG).
* '''Phase-Field Mechanics:''' Ideal for modeling continuous vacuum state transitions, domain walls, and topological field boundaries.

== Strategic Role in SVD ==
FiPy provides the continuous flux-conserving simulation layer for evaluating vacuum phase transitions and scalar-vector field couplings.
